for_davis: Fable 5.2 is the model his Claude Code sessions run on — cheaper, faster, and now with a fast mode for long agent runs — and the IPO wobble is the market context for the career he's entering: the lab he builds on is about to become a public company, and its valuation is being repriced in real time.
headline: Fable 5.2 lands cheaper and faster, Anthropic's $69B IPO wobbles, and agent compute gets a price cut

stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Nov 9 — the same underlying model, split by safeguards. Fable is generally available; Mythos, with cyber and biology safeguards lifted, goes only to vetted organizations through Anthropic's verification programs. Both are priced at $8/$40 per million tokens, down from $10/$50, run up to 30% faster, and offer an optional fast mode at 2.5x speed for $16/$80. Anthropic says Fable 5.2 coordinated 1,000+ agents over eight days to build a working operating system, and designed three working electronic devices.
stories.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ship: same model, split by safeguards, 20% cheaper
stories.why_it_matters: Fable is the model his Claude Code sessions run on — cheaper, faster, and now with a fast mode for the long agent runs his project work needs.

stories.summary: Anthropic circulated IPO pricing to bankers on Monday — about 867 million shares at $70–$80, raising up to $69.3B — then emailed hours later calling the details inaccurate and promising an update. A revised draft seen by Reuters on Tuesday prices shares at $70–$78 for up to $64.4B, with the roadshow expected to begin Tuesday and trading possibly as early as Nov 19–20. The backdrop: a reported $3.4B deal for 1.7 GW of gas generators to power data centers, and about $895B in disclosed infrastructure commitments.
stories.title: Anthropic's $69.3B IPO pricing circulates, then gets retracted within hours
stories.why_it_matters: The lab he builds on is about to become a public company — its valuation, now talked at $1.2–1.3T against ~$2T earlier, sets the hiring and spending climate for his whole transition.

stories.summary: Meta introduced Muse Ember on Nov 9, the compact, low-latency member of its proprietary Muse model family, aimed at tool calls, routing and repeated agent tasks. On the Meta Model API it costs $0.10 per million uncached input tokens ($0.004 cached) and $0.50 per million output tokens. Meta's Muse shopping agent is also reportedly heading to the UK within weeks, with retailer partnerships to let it make purchases; Meta declined to comment on that timing.
stories.title: Meta's Muse Ember: ten cents a million tokens for repetitive agent work
stories.why_it_matters: Agent-task compute at ten cents a million tokens changes the unit economics of the follow-up agent he's building — the per-call cost is heading toward negligible.

stories.summary: Google announced TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max on Nov 9, bringing its eighth-generation TPU lineup to four configurations. Google positions 8tx for confidential inference with sensitive data and model weights, and 8i Max for large context windows and memory-intensive agent workloads. Pricing and availability dates remain undisclosed; Bloomberg reported the expanded lineup intensifies Google's competition with NVIDIA.
stories.title: Google adds TPU 8tx and 8i Max, aimed squarely at agent workloads
stories.why_it_matters: The hardware race is now explicitly about agent workloads — large contexts and memory-heavy inference — which is what makes his multi-agent builds affordable to run.

stories.summary: OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise purchasable through AWS Marketplace, so organizations can buy it through existing AWS billing and apply spending toward AWS commitments. Separately, OpenAI introduced Control Room, an internal system that monitors AI research workloads and can halt model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene.
stories.title: ChatGPT Enterprise lands on AWS Marketplace; OpenAI builds a 35-second kill switch
stories.why_it_matters: Enterprise AI is now bought like cloud infrastructure — through the marketplace — and the 35-second halt switch is the governance pattern his own agent's approval flow should mirror.

tldr: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Nov 9 — same model, split by safeguards, $8/$40 per million tokens and up to 30% faster — while its IPO pricing was circulated to bankers and retracted within hours, with a revised draft now aiming at up to $64.4B. Meta launched Muse Ember at $0.10/$0.50 for repetitive agent work, Google added two eighth-gen TPUs, OpenAI put ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace, and six governments plus the major labs signed a Paris safety declaration.
